initial: A 12-year-old female presented with asymptomatic vulvar edema of 1 month's duration that was previously treated with topical antifungals and corticosteroids with no improvement. She did not report recent travel or sexual relationships. Medical history included growth delay, several months of constipation treated with laxatives, and hemorrhoids.

exams.source_report: Examination revealed swelling, erythema, and palpable induration on the labia minora and majora of the vulva. No lymphadenopathy was palpated in the inguinal region.

tests.source_report: - Laboratory tests: Slight increase in erythrocyte sedimentation rate, normal angiotensin-converting enzyme levels, negative interferon γ release assay. Fecal calprotectin was 297 μg/g (normal <50 μg/g). Negative stool culture and parasite studies.- Imaging studies:  - Chest radiography: Normal  - Intestinal and pelvic MRI: Normal  - Endoscopic study: Revealed ulcers in duodenal bulb, rectum, sigmoid colon, terminal ileum, and cecum. Erythematous and edematous mucosa with aphthous ulcers in sigmoid and rectal region.- Pathology:  - 4mm punch biopsy from right labia majora showed:    Image Description: Intact epidermis with nodular dermatitis composed of non-necrotizing granulomas in superficial and deep dermis  - Additional histological findings: Aggregated nodules of epithelioid histiocytes without necrosis, poorly compact granulomas with ill-defined borders, associated lymphocytic and eosinophilic infiltrate  - Gastric and intestinal endoscopic biopsies: Granulomas in lamina propria not linked to active crypt injury

initial: A 40-year-old man from eastern India presented with a nonhealing ulcer on the tongue present for the last 4 months. The lesion started as a small painless mass on the right lateral aspect of the tongue, which gradually grew and subsequently ulcerated. It caused mild difficulty in eating. No history of trauma or tongue bite preceding the lesion. Patient denied consuming tobacco or alcohol regularly. Medical history includes well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus for 2 years with oral hypoglycemic agents. No systemic complaints. No history of high-risk behavior for HIV.

exams.source_report: Single well-defined ulcer measuring 2 × 2 cm on the right lateral aspect of tongue with a clean base and irregular and elevated heaped-up margins. No underlying induration, friability, or bleeding on manipulation. Rest of the oral cavity was normal.

tests.source_report: - Histopathological examination (3-mm punch biopsy from edge of ulcer):  - Dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, epithelioid cells, giant cells, plasma cells, eosinophils, and neutrophils  - Many histiocytes and giant cells contained intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo  - Special stains (Grocott-Gomori methenamine-silver nitrate and periodic acid–Schiff) highlighted fungal forms  - Fungal culture on Sabouraud dextrose agar was negative  - HIV-1 and HIV-2 serologic testing were negativeImages:- Figure 1A Title: Tongue ulcer- Figure 1B Title: Biopsy from the ulcer showing a mixed cell infiltrate (hematoxylin-eosin, original magnification ×40)- Figure 1C Title: Intracellular yeast forms within the histiocytes (original magnification ×100)

initial: An adult patient with morbid obesity and otherwise no significant medical history presented with progressive headache, double vision, and blurry vision over the past year, which acutely worsened over the past 2 months. Concurrent decreased libido and erectile dysfunction were reported.

exams.source_report: Ophthalmologic examination revealed bilateral optic nerve atrophy, profound bitemporal visual field loss, and nonreactive pupils.

initial: A woman in her 70s presented with a week of painless, rapidly progressive, edematous, necrotic papules and plaques on the extremities, buttocks, and face with sharp demarcation at the nasolabial folds and extension into the oral mucosa. Notable symptoms included 4 months of extreme fatigue, 20.4 kg weight loss, and a recent episode of hematochezia. Medical history included diabetes, hyperlipidemia, and hypertension that were well controlled with simvastatin, chlorthalidone, hydralazine hydrochloride, lisinopril, and verapamil hydrochloride for 5 years with no new exposures. Age-appropriate cancer screening was up to date.

exams.source_report: Patient was afebrile and hemodynamically stable. Examination showed edematous, ulcerated pink plaques confluent on forehead and cheeks with sharp demarcation at nasolabial fold. Retiform purpuric plaque was present on the left leg with overlying desquamation. On hospital day 2, she developed bright red blood per rectum.

tests.source_report: - Laboratory findings: Leukocytosis, normocytic anemia, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, hematuria, and proteinuria. Rheumatological workup showed positive antinuclear antibody titer (1:160), antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody with perinuclear staining (1:1280), myeloperoxidase antibody level of 103 AU/mL, serine proteinase 3 antibody level of 25 AU/mL, and antihistone antibody level of 2.2 U. Negative for double-stranded DNA antibody and antiphospholipid syndrome antibody panel.- Imaging studies: Computed tomography of chest, abdomen, and pelvis revealed parenchymal lung nodules.- Pathology:   Image Title: Skin Biopsy Findings  Image Description: Histological examination revealed a neutrophil-rich infiltrate in a predominately perivascular pattern with extravasated erythrocytes, leukocytoclasis with karyorrhectic debris, fibrinoid degeneration of vessels walls, and cryptococcoid forms. Microbial stains (periodic acid–Schiff, Grocott methenamine silver, Gram, and acid-fast bacillus) and tissue cultures were unremarkable.    Lung biopsy showed reactive inflammation and was negative for malignant neoplasm.

initial: A woman in her 40s presented with a well-circumscribed, pigmented, episcleral lesion in her right eye. Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/16 OD.

exams.source_report: Well-circumscribed, pigmented, episcleral lesion observed in the right eye.

tests.source_report: - Ultrasound biomicroscopy: Showed extension of a dome-shaped primary ciliary body tumor. Revealed adjacent ciliary body tumor with a ciliary artery channel connecting the intrascleral and extrascleral tumor portions.  - Standardized A-scan echography: Showed medium internal reflectivity.  - Biopsy findings: Well-circumscribed, pigmented, spindle cell tumor with small nuclei showing homogeneous chromatin distribution, lack of mitotic figures, and strong immunopositivity for melan A.  - Images:  Figure A Title: Pigmented episcleral tumor  Figure A Description: Pigmented, well-delineated episcleral tumor in the right eye    Figure B Title: Transversal epigraphic section  Figure B Description: Shows adjacent ciliary body tumor with a ciliary artery channel connecting the intrascleral and extrascleral tumor portions

initial: A man in his 70s presented to the emergency department with progressive dyspnea on exertion. His medical history includes multiple prior cardiac events and lung cancer with metastatic disease to the brain and myocardium. Ten months prior, he had received 2 drug-eluting stents to the right coronary artery. At presentation, the patient denied chest pain.

exams.source_report: No detailed physical examination findings were provided in the case report.

tests.source_report: - Laboratory tests: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin-T (hs-cTnT) level was 40 ng/L (reference range, 0-14 ng/L), unchanged from baseline value obtained 1 month prior.- ECG findings:   - Normal sinus rhythm at 90 beats per minute  - 1.0-mm ST elevation in lead V1  - 4.0-mm ST elevation in leads V2 and V3   - T-wave inversions in leads I, aVL, V4, V5, and V6  - Diffusely low voltages in both limb leads and precordial leads  - Imaging studies:  1. Transthoracic echocardiogram:     Image Title: Apical 4-chamber view     Image Description: Well-circumscribed 2.8 × 2.6-cm mass located in the left ventricular mid-apical anteroseptum     Additional findings:      - Preserved left ventricular systolic function     - No regional wall motion abnormalities     - Large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade  2. Coronary angiography:     Findings: Nonobstructive epicardial coronary artery disease without evidence of acute thrombotic or embolic occlusion

initial: A highly functioning man in his 80s with a history of Parkinson disease and atopic dermatitis presented to the emergency department. He had severe intractable pruritus that was resistant to multiple standard treatments. Four days prior, he was prescribed mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) 500mg twice daily and a topical medication composed of 10% ketamine, 5% amitriptyline, and 5% lidocaine (KAL) in lipoderm base to be used twice daily. After initial application to small test areas showed improvement, he gradually increased coverage to most of his upper body the evening before presentation.

exams.source_report: The patient presented with:- Slurred speech- Ataxia - Altered mental status- Persistently nonfocal findings on neurological examination- Oscillating level of consciousness consistent with delirium

tests.source_report: - Toxicology:  Mass spectroscopy-based urine toxicology test detected:  - Amitriptyline and metabolites  - Lidocaine and metabolites    - Ketamine (2360 ng/mL; normal level: 0 ng/mL) and metabolites including norketamine

initial: A man in his 80s presented for his 1-month follow-up after bioprosthetic aortic valve placement. Medical history includes paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, first degree atrioventricular block, and sick sinus syndrome with a dual-chamber permanent pacemaker placed a year prior. The pacemaker's lower rate limit had been increased from 60 bpm to 80 bpm perioperatively and was decreased back to 60 bpm two weeks before presentation. At presentation, he was feeling well and denied chest pain or dyspnea.

exams.source_report: No specific physical examination findings were reported in the case.

tests.source_report: - ECG at presentation: Shows sinus rhythm at 76 bpm, first-degree atrioventricular block, and deep symmetric T-wave inversions across precordial leads (V1-V6) and inferior leads (II, III, and aVF).- Baseline ECG (2 weeks prior): Shows underlying atrial fibrillation with ventricular pacing at 80 bpm. QRS complexes were 198 milliseconds wide and negatively directed with upright T waves in precordial and inferior leads.- Transthoracic echocardiogram: Shows normal left ventricular size and function, no wall motion abnormalities, and a well-seated bioprosthetic valve in the aortic position.- Follow-up ECG (1 month later): Shows recurrent atrial fibrillation with right ventricular-paced rhythm at 60 bpm and discordant T waves.Images mentioned:1. Title: Figure 1. Electrocardiogram Obtained at Presentation2. Title: Figure 2. Electrocardiogram Obtained 2 Weeks Prior to Presentation

initial: A patient in their 30s with obesity and a history of alcohol use was found to have recurrent arrhythmia during hospitalization. The patient had a prolonged hospital stay complicated by delirium tremens, intubation, and ventilator-associated pneumonia requiring multiple courses of antibiotics. Two weeks prior, the patient had undergone insertion of a peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC) and tracheostomy. The arrhythmia episodes were particularly noticeable when the patient assumed a left lateral decubitus position, associated with palpitations but without chest pain, dyspnea, presyncope or hemodynamic compromise.

exams.source_report: Two-dimensional echocardiography showed normal left ventricular function without structural abnormalities.

initial: An 11-year-old boy underwent bilateral tympanostomy tube placement (beveled Armstrong type) and adenoidectomy for recurrent acute otitis media despite prior placement of tympanostomy tubes. The day after surgery, he developed symptoms requiring emergency department evaluation. He had multiple hospital visits over several days with a persistent cough that continued even while sleeping. The cough was dry and occurred with every breath. Previous treatments with albuterol, intravenous lorazepam, beclometasone dipropionate, and promethazine with codeine were ineffective.

exams.source_report: Patient presented with stridor and increased work of breathing initially. Later developed intermittent low-pitched, biphasic stridor. No fever, congestion, malaise, or other signs of upper respiratory illness were present.

tests.source_report: - Flexible laryngoscopy: Normal findings- Respiratory virus panel: Negative- Diagnostic microlaryngoscopy and bronchoscopy: Revealed a normal airway- Image Title: Course of the Auricular Branch of the Vagus Nerve (Arnold Nerve), Right Ear View  Image Description: Illustration showing the auricular branch of the vagus nerve originating from the inferior ganglion of the glossopharyngeal nerve and superior ganglion of the vagus nerve, ascending from the jugular foramen to the mastoid process via the mastoid canaliculus

initial: A man in his 70s with history of atrial flutter treated with metoprolol succinate (without anticoagulation), heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes. He presented with intermittent palpitations and dyspnea occurring daily for 1 month, most consistently triggered by anxiety. On the morning of admission, the patient experienced another episode with persistently elevated heart rate.

exams.source_report: Vital signs:- Afebrile- Heart rate: 136 beats per minute- Blood pressure: 147/96 mm HgPhysical findings:- Tachycardia- Faint bibasilar crackles on lung examinationLater findings:- Blood pressure dropped to 70/30-79/39 mm Hg range

tests.source_report: Electrocardiogram (ECG) findings:Initial ECG:- Typical atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction- After amiodarone: Heart rate decreased to 126 bpm with 2:1 conductionLater ECG:- Wide QRS (>120 ms) complex tachycardia- Heart rate: 252 bpm- Right precordial leads: rsR′ pattern- Limb leads: left axis deviation- Unable to reliably identify P waves- Atrial rate equal to ventricular rate (252 activations per minute)Subsequent Testing:- Invasive electrophysiology study revealed sustained, typical atrial flutter with no inducible ventricular tachycardia

initial: A 17-month-old boy presented with a slow-growing, nontender plaque on the lower back. The plaque was initially 1 × 1 cm and had grown with the child. Medical history included dermal melanocytosis of the right hip and mid back, increased head circumference (97th percentile), and expressive language delay. No family history of congenital birthmarks.

exams.source_report: Well-appearing boy with normal vital signs and Fitzpatrick type III skin type. On the left lower back, there was a 15 × 5-cm indurated skin-colored to yellow, firm, multinodular plaque with hypertrichosis, extending from the midline to the left lower flank. Additional blue-gray patches were present on the back and right hip, as well as a small café au lait macule on the right lower back. Limited neurologic examination was within normal limits.

tests.source_report: - Biopsy findings:    - Hematoxylin-eosin staining showed diffuse dermal infiltration of spindle cells, predominantly encircling terminal folliculosebaceous units    - Higher-power magnification revealed mix of partially fusiform melanocytes and dendritic cells with glassy, eosinophilic cytoplasm    - Immunohistochemical staining showed diffuse and periadnexal S100 positivity in the mid to deep dermis    - Additional staining: Positive for CD34, SOX-10; Negative for desmin, SMA, CD1a; Partial expression of Melan A and epithelial membrane antigen  - Imaging:    - MRI of lumbar spine showed contrast-enhancing cutaneous lesion extending between L3-L5 spinal segment    - Branches of enhancement extending into paraspinous soft tissues of L4 and deep subcutaneous tissues of L3 spinous process    - No evidence of spinal involvement or dysraphism  Images included:  Figure A: Large, well-defined, firm yellow to skin-colored multinodular hypertrichotic plaque on the left lower back  Figure B: Hematoxylin-eosin staining of dermal infiltration (×4 magnification)  Figure C: Higher-power magnification of melanocytes and dendritic cells (×40 magnification)  Figure D: Immunohistochemical S100 staining (×4 magnification)

initial: A woman in her 80s with a history of nonischemic cardiomyopathy and chronic kidney disease presented with purpuric lesions on her face, elbows, knees, and feet. She was initially admitted for altered mental status in the setting of an unwitnessed fall and was noted to have 'bruises' on her lower extremities. New lesions developed on her nose, ear, and the extensor surfaces of her arms bilaterally.

exams.source_report: The patient's nose, bilateral cheeks, forehead, and left ear (helical rim and antihelix) were found to have dusky purpuric macules and patches. Her knees, feet, and the extensor surfaces of her arms had reticulated purpuric macules and patches. There was skin sloughing off the lesions on her elbows and knees.

tests.source_report: - Laboratory tests:     - Hypercalcemia (calcium level, 11.5 mg/dL)    - Acute kidney injury (creatinine level, 5.6 mg/dL)    - Rouleaux and cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear    - Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses    - Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis    - Elevated serum cryoglobulin levels (cryocrit, 16%)    - Negative results for hepatitis, antinuclear antibodies, rheumatoid factor, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia antibodies, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies  - Biopsy findings:    Four-millimeter punch biopsy specimens from left ear, right arm, and forehead showed multifocal intravascular fibrinoid material consisting of a mix of cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi with relatively little vessel wall inflammation  - Imaging studies:    CT scan of pelvis revealed lytic bony lesions      - Bone marrow biopsy:    Hypercellular marrow consisting of 80% plasma cells with atypical morphology and κ-light-chain restriction

initial: A healthy young woman presented with a 2-month history of an enlarging right anterior thigh subcutaneous mass. The lesion was asymptomatic but had grown significantly. She ran recreationally and recalled no trauma to the area.

exams.source_report: A 4-cm firm subcutaneous mass was palpated with no overlying epidermal change. The mass was palpable with right hip flexion and disappeared on right hip extension.

tests.source_report: - Laboratory tests: Complete blood cell count and lactate dehydrogenase test results were normal.- Imaging studies:  1. Plain-film radiography of the right femur was normal.  2. initial: A male patient in their early 50s with no history of prior known diseases was admitted with epigastric pain and jaundice of 2 weeks. On the third day of admission, the patient experienced a sudden squeezing pain in the anterior chest at rest, with a heart rate of 44 beats/min, blood pressure of 97/60 mm Hg, and oxygen saturation of 98%. During hospitalization, the patient experienced recurrent episodes of precordial pain 17 times in the following days, with similar pain characteristics as before.

exams.source_report: Initial ECG findings at admission were normal. During chest pain episode: Heart rate 44 beats/min, blood pressure 97/60 mm Hg, oxygen saturation 98%.

tests.source_report: - ECG Studies:    Image A Title: ECG During Chest Pain Attack    Image A Description: Complete atrioventricular block with 4-5mm ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF; 3-6mm ST-segment depression in leads I, aVL, and V1 through V5    Image B Title: ECG After Chest Pain Relief     Image B Description: Normal findings with 53 beats per minute  - Laboratory Tests:    - Troponin I: 0.107 ng/mL (normal: 0-0.034 ng/mL)    - Total bilirubin: 14.08 mg/dL (normal: 0.30-2.92 mg/dL)  - Imaging Studies:    - Echocardiography: Normal cardiac structure and systolic function    - Coronary angiography: Mild nonobstructive disease    - Endoscopic biopsy and PET-CT: Revealed malignant duodenal tumor with peripancreatic metastasis    - Surgical findings: 8 × 6 × 5-cm mass at pancreaticoduodenal junction, upper part invading gallbladder

initial: An 83-year-old woman presented since 2006 with a generalized pruritic eruption comprising annular and polycyclic plaques on the face, neck, trunk, and extremities with changing appearance. The patient was evaluated and received care at Ciudad Real University General Hospital beginning in 2014.

exams.source_report: Erythematous annular, semilunar and polycyclic plaques were observed on the back. The lesions were pruritic in nature.

tests.source_report: - Laboratory tests: Complete blood cell count was normal, routine biochemistry profile was normal, and serum immunoglobulin E levels were normal. Antinuclear antibodies and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies were negative.- Imaging studies: Full-body computed tomography scan showed no abnormalities.- Pathological examination:   Image Title: Biopsy Specimens Before Treatment  Image Description: Showed superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial lymphocytic inflammation with numerous eosinophils

initial: A patient in their 60s was admitted to the intensive care unit for gastrointestinal bleeding and shock. Medical history includes liver cirrhosis and portal hypertension with ruptured esophageal varices. Despite fluid resuscitation and pressors, blood pressure continued to fall and kidney function progressively deteriorated.

exams.source_report: Patient presented with profound hypotension and shock.

tests.source_report: - ECG Findings:    - Initial 12-lead ECG showed:      - Sinus tachycardia at 115 beats per minute      - Upright P waves in most leads, negative and biphasic P waves in V1 and V2      - Normal PR interval      - QRS complexes slightly widened at 120 milliseconds      - Slightly atypical right bundle-branch block pattern in V1 and V2      - Right superior QRS axis      - Computer interpretation showed ventricular rate of 230 bpm (double the true rate)        - Follow-up Telemetry (40 minutes later):      - Very slow wide-complex rhythm without P waves      - QRS complexes widened to approximately 180 ms      - Prominent and tented T waves      - True ventricular rate 26-30 bpm (computer calculated 61 bpm)        - Laboratory Tests:      - Serum potassium level > 9.0 mmol/L (normal: 3.6-5.4 mmol/L)

initial: A man in his 80s presented with a 4-month history of new-onset persistent facial eruption. Medical history includes pacemaker, congestive heart failure, coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, transient ischemic attack, and Parkinson disease. Patient is dependent in all activities of daily living. He denied a history of facial flushing. Previous treatment with topical 1% metronidazole cream for 1 month showed no improvement, and he developed acute facial purpura after 1 day of oral doxycycline, which was discontinued.

exams.source_report: Patient had asymmetric, centrofacial, erythematous-violaceous indurated telangiectatic and ecchymotic plaques over a phymatous background.

tests.source_report: - Histopathologic examination: Revealed a dissecting vascular proliferation through the entire dermis. Ectatic vascular channels were lined by atypical plump endothelial cells.  - Immunohistochemistry: Negative for Human herpesvirus 8.  - PET/CT scan: Revealed mildly avid malar subcutaneous thickening.Images:- Image A Title: Clinical image  Description: Erythemato-violaceous plaques with ecchymotic areas  - Image B Title: Histopathologic image  Description: Ectatic vessels with plump endothelia involving the deep dermis and hypodermis (hemotoxylin-eosin)  - Image C Title: Higher magnification histopathologic image  Description: Ectatic vascular channels lined by atypical plump endothelial cells (hemotoxylin-eosin)  - Image D Title: Immunohistochemistry  Description: Negative for Human herpesvirus 8 (original magnification ×100)

initial: A man in his 20s presented to the emergency department with 1 day of chest pressure. Four days prior to presentation he experienced subjective fevers, rhinorrhea, a dry cough, and sinus congestion. The day prior to presentation he experienced 3 hours of substernal pressure that resolved spontaneously. In the early morning of the day of presentation, he was awakened from sleep by constant chest pressure radiating to the right jaw, diaphoresis, and 1 episode of vomiting. He reported no medical history.

exams.source_report: Vital signs obtained in the Emergency Department were within normal limits. Cardiac examination revealed a regular rate and rhythm, normal point of maximum impulse without lifts, and no murmurs, rubs, or gallops in supine, sitting, or standing positions. The remainder of the physical examination was within normal limits.

tests.source_report:
- Laboratory Tests:
  * Initial serum troponin I level: 6.18 ng/mL
  * Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein (values increased over next 3 days)

- Imaging and Other Tests:
  * ECG Findings: Normal sinus rhythm, ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression in leads II, III, and aVF, ST-segment depression in lead V1, and PR-segment elevation in lead aVR
  * Coronary angiography: Normal coronary arteries, left ventricular end-diastolic pressure 12 mm Hg (reference range, 4-12 mm Hg)
  * Transthoracic echocardiogram: Normal results

initial: A school-aged boy presented with occasionally pruritic, generalized hyperkeratotic papules with central white spicules and comedo-like plugs in a linear distribution on his face, trunk, and extremities since birth. Some eruptions on his trunk had spontaneously resolved with developmental growth. There was nonconsanguineous marriage of his parents, and no family members had similar lesions. The patient was otherwise in good general health and without developmental delay.

exams.source_report: Generalized, linear hyperkeratotic papules with numerous central small filiform keratotic white spicules and brown plugs on the head, face, neck, trunk, and bilateral upper and lower extremities, including palms and soles along Blaschko lines, accompanied with alopecia of the scalp and eyebrows. The examination of nails, mucosae, and teeth was unremarkable. No extracutaneous involvement was observed.

tests.source_report: - Dermoscopic examination:     - Face: Many central white spines    - Right palm: Brown cores surrounded by yellow crater-like rings  - Skin biopsy (from right thigh):    Image Title: Histopathological examination    Image Description: Shows hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, and parakeratotic columns overlying the dilated epidermal invaginations, as well as thinner granular layers and dilated eccrine ostia and acrosyringia under the parakeratotic columns (hematoxylin-eosin)  - Clinical Images:    Image A: Generalized, linear hyperkeratotic papules and plaques with numerous white spicules and plugs on the head, face, neck, and both arms with alopecia of scalp and eyebrows    Image B: Close-up view of generalized hyperkeratotic papules with numerous central small filiform keratotic white spicules on the face    Image C: Dermoscopic view showing many central whitish spines on the face

initial: A girl younger than 2 years presented with a 1-year history of slightly pruritic lesions involving her face. She was born after an uncomplicated pregnancy and delivery, and her growth and development were appropriate for her age. No associated symptoms such as fever, anorexia, or weight loss were noted.

exams.source_report: Multiple skin-colored and erythematous follicular papules, 1 to 2 mm in diameter, distributed in a segmental pattern on the right side of the forehead, as well as the dorsum and tip of the nose. A small, excoriated plaque was noted on the right malar area. No mucosal lesions were present, and the rest of the physical examination findings were unremarkable.

initial: A woman in her 60s presented with a 3-month history of pain, swelling, and erythema on her face. Medical history includes left breast carcinoma diagnosed eleven years earlier, treated with mastectomy, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy. Seven years after initial diagnosis, she had left supraclavicular lymph nodes metastasis treated with surgical excision. Current symptoms include pain on palpation, with no fever or chills.

exams.source_report: Violaceous swelling with telangiectasia and necrosis on the forehead, eyelids, nose, and cheek, predominantly involving the left side of the face.

tests.source_report: - Histopathological examination:  Findings: Hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and dilated vessels in the dermis. initial: A woman in her late 20s presented with an asymptomatic hyperpigmentation on the right side of the trunk, right upper arm, and right leg, strictly following the lines of Blaschko. A slight atrophy of the hyperpigmented skin was palpable without any signs of induration. The first onset was in her childhood, at age 6 years, with a small hyperpigmentation on the right side of her lower chest remaining stable for years. In her early 20s the area of hyperpigmentation started to spread slowly over the above-mentioned areas and became more intense.

exams.source_report: Slightly atrophic hyperpigmented macules following the lines of Blaschko on the right side of the trunk and upper arm. The hyperpigmented skin showed slight atrophy on palpation without induration.

initial: A homosexual man presented with an ulcerative lesion on his penis of 2 months' duration. He had consulted several dermatologists and received different local and systemic treatments including antibiotics, steroids, and antimycotic drugs, with no improvement. The patient had a stable partner and denied both casual and unprotected sex as well as the use of creams or balms on the penis. During counseling, the patient reported using a substance called 'Jungle Juice' during sexual encounters, and could not rule out accidental contact between his contaminated hands and his genitals.

exams.source_report: The shaft of the penis had an asymptomatic, oval ulcer of more than 3 cm on its long axis with undermined borders and a sanious reddish bottom.

tests.source_report:
- Serological Tests: Antibody screening for syphilis and HIV - negative results
- Microbiological Tests: Screening for common bacteria and yeasts - negative results
- PCR Testing: Tests for Treponema and Chlamydia species - negative results
- Histologic Analysis: Full epidermal necrosis with infiltration of neutrophils and eosinophils. A diffuse dermal inflammatory infiltrate rich in polymorphonucleocytes, and focal fibrinoid necrosis of superficial vessels
- Patch Testing: International Contact Dermatitis Research Group standard series and single patch test with alkyl nitrite preparation at 2% in water - negative at 48 and 72 hours

initial: A woman in her mid-20s with common variable immune deficiency (CVID) for 11 years, with history of frequent infectious disease and autoimmune conditions including dermatitis, pancreatitis, colitis, cerebritis, and lung disease. She was managed with antibiotics, corticosteroids, and immune globulin therapy. For 3 weeks, she noted bilateral ocular pain and blurred vision.

exams.source_report: Visual acuity was 20/200 OD and 20/25 OS. The anterior segment, vitreous, and retina demonstrated no inflammation. Ophthalmoscopy revealed multifocal choroidal infiltrates in each eye. Right eye infiltration measured 14 mm at base, 3.9-mm thickness, with overlying subretinal fluid plus additional tiny multifocal sites. Left eye showed multifocal small choroidal infiltrates of 0.5-mm diameter.

tests.source_report: - Biopsy: Transvitreous fine-needle aspiration biopsy of macular lesion in right eye showed scant lymphocytes and histiocytes, with no evidence of fungus, bacteria, or malignant cells.- Microbiological studies: Tests of tumor aspirate, blood, and urine samples showed no infection.- Imaging:  Image Title: Figure 1. Autoimmune Choroidopathy  Image Description: A-D shows choroidopathy on ophthalmoscopy. E and F show optical coherence tomography findings.  Image Title: Figure 2. Resolution After Treatment  Image Description: Findings after 3 months showing resolution of choroidal infiltration, with chorioretinal scar at biopsy site in right eye, less apparent focal choroidal inflammatory sites in left eye, resolution of subretinal fluid with residual precipitates in right eye, and normal findings in left eye.

initial: A man in his 40s presented with a 2-year history of multiple asymptomatic lesions on the face and neck. The lesions were round, hypopigmented macules and were symmetrically distributed in the affected area. The macules had appeared on his cheeks 2 years earlier and had gradually coalesced. The size of the lesions ranged from approximately 2 to 3 mm to 25 mm in diameter. There was no hair growth at the site of the lesions, and the patient reported no symptoms. He was previously treated for tinea versicolor, without success.

exams.source_report: Multiple round, hypopigmented macules symmetrically distributed on face and neck. Lesions ranged from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter. Absence of hair growth in affected areas.

tests.source_report: - Skin Biopsy Results:    - Histopathologic findings showed plate-like subepidermal tumor extending horizontally under epidermis with multiple cord-like connections to overlying epidermis    - Neoplastic cords consisted of clear/pale epithelial cells with cytoplasm showing strong periodic acid-Schiff staining due to glycogen accumulation    - Stroma formed by fibrous connective tissue    - Marked elastosis observed in dermis surrounding tumor  Images:    Image A Title: Hypopigmented macules on the face and neck    Image B Title: Absence of hair growth in the affected area    Image C Title: Hematoxylin-eosin staining (original magnification ×10)    Image D Title: Hematoxylin-eosin staining (original magnification ×20)

initial: A man in his 70s presented for evaluation of a nonhealing lesion of his left cheek. His barber had noted increased difficulty trimming hair around his auricles due to their inflexibility. Medical history included type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension and secondary chronic renal insufficiency, cardiovascular disease, and gout. Current medications included lisinopril, glipizide, terazosin, insulin glargine, labetalol, allopurinol, hydrochlorothiazide, and erythropoietin.

exams.source_report: Examination of the head and neck revealed bilateral auricular rigidity and immobility. Both ears appeared normal and were nontender and asymptomatic. Increased rigidity of nasal cartilage was noted. Patient denied any decrease in auditory acuity, frostbite, or previous trauma to his ears.

initial: A 13-month-old girl was referred for evaluation of an asymptomatic, solid nasopharyngeal mass found incidentally on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) obtained for evaluation of a morning glory disc anomaly at age 11 months. The patient was asymptomatic and had normal hormone levels including insulin-like growth factor 1, thyroid-stimulating hormone, free thyroxine, and adrenocorticotropic hormone.

exams.source_report: Flexible fiberoptic nasopharyngoscopy through the nares revealed a smooth, pedunculated lesion predominantly obstructing the right choana and adherent to the posterior pharyngeal wall by a stalk. The pedunculated mass appeared distinctly separate from adjacent sessile adenoid tissue. Follow-up examination showed the mass ball-valving into the right choana and partially obstructing the left choana.

tests.source_report: - Imaging Studies:    MRI revealed a minimally enhancing rounded 5-mm soft-tissue mass along the roof of the right nasopharynx, distinct from adjacent adenoid tissue. The sella turcica was small and abnormally shaped, with a persistently patent craniopharyngeal canal measuring 2 mm superiorly. Additional tissue was evident inferiorly within the craniopharyngeal canal.        Image Title: Sagittal T1 MRI without contrast    Image Description: A 5-mm nasopharyngeal mass visible at 11 months of age        Image Title: T1-weighted MRI with contrast (6-month follow-up)    Image Description: Minimally enhancing mass unchanged, with patent craniopharyngeal canal showing bright signal of enhancing tissue within  - Laboratory Tests:    Normal levels of:    - Insulin-like growth factor 1    - Thyroid-stimulating hormone    - Free thyroxine     - Adrenocorticotropic hormone

initial: A 34-year old African American woman with a history of nodular sclerosing type stage IIE Hodgkin lymphoma (treated with 4 cycles of ABVC followed by 3060 cGY at the neck and mediastinum) presented with a painless, left upper eyelid mass that had previously been excised on 3 separate occasions outside of our institution. Four months later, the patient presented with painless proptosis. After subsequent treatments, the patient presented with left-sided facial numbness seventeen months later.

exams.source_report: Initial presentation showed a left upper eyelid mass. Later examinations revealed proptosis.

tests.source_report: - Histopathology: Revealed a multinodular proliferation of osteoclastlike multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells demonstrating increased mitotic activity. Immunohistochemistry was positive for CD68 and negative for CD45, S100, desmin, and lysozyme.- Imaging Studies:  Image Title: MRI of the orbits  Image Description: Axial T1-weighted fat-saturated postgadolinium MRI shows lesion with marked interval enlargement within the orbit and extension through the frontal sinus into the intracranial compartment  Image Title: MRI of the skull base  Image Description: Axial T1-weighted postgadolinium MRI shows tumor centered at the left cavernous sinus and orbital apex involving the left intracavernous/supraclinoid segments of the internal carotid artery with extension into the right cavernous sinus and right sphenoid sinus and with mass effect on the left temporal lobe- Genetic Testing: Next-generation sequencing of the tumor demonstrated a splicing variant (c.2515-1G>A) in the partner and localizer of BRCA2 (PALB2)

initial: A 2-year-old girl who was otherwise healthy presented with a 10-month history of asymptomatic skin depressions in her neck, nape, and submandibular regions. The lesion initially occurred as an erythema in the neck and progressed centrifugally to the nape and submandibular areas. Her medical and family histories were unremarkable. Her parents denied drug injection or trauma history.

exams.source_report: Atrophy was observed in the center of the lesion, surrounded by an erythematous border, with underlying blood vessels being visible deep to the atrophy. Cervical lymph nodes were palpable bilaterally. Tactile responses within the depressed as well as surrounding areas were normal. Other physical examinations were without abnormalities.

Cervical lymph nodes slightly enlarged bilaterally

initial: A patient in their 20s presented to the emergency department complaining of severe midsternal chest pain of several hours' duration. The patient was in very good health before their presentation. The patient was not taking any medications and had no risk factors for coronary artery disease. They used cocaine 3 to 4 hours before presentation.

exams.source_report: Patient was thin, anxious, and in acute distress. The patient was diaphoretic and tachypneic. Blood pressure was 138/80 mm Hg with a regular pulse of 180 beats per minute; no fever. The patient had a questionable S4, but otherwise their examination was unremarkable.

initial: A healthy woman in her 60s presented with multiple erythematous crusted plaques on her trunk that had appeared 4 weeks previously, sparing her limbs and facial region. She had a long-standing history of several outbreaks of skin lesions limited to both axillae and groin. Previous episodes had been successfully treated with various topical drugs administered by her primary care physician. No family history of similar lesions was recorded.

exams.source_report: Multiple annular erythematous plaques surrounded by a peripheral crusted and pustular collarette on her trunk. No active lesions were present in her axillae, inframammary folds, or groin.

initial: A man in his early 50s with a history of human immunodeficiency virus, type 1 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia presented for a routine diabetic screening examination without ophthalmic complaints. He had a history of infection 10 years prior to presentation, which was treated with oral penicillin. His rapid plasma reagin was nonreactive 1 year prior to presentation.

exams.source_report: Visual acuity was 20/20 − 3 OD and 20/20 − 1 OS. Anterior segment and vitreous were unremarkable without inflammation in both eyes. Dilated ophthalmoscopy revealed a neurosensory detachment in the inferior macula of the right eye including the fovea. Subretinal yellow lesions smaller than 100 μm in diameter were present, as was slightly elevated, poorly demarcated yellow discoloration in the central portion of the neurosensory detachment. The left fundus was within normal limits.

initial: A young black woman presented with painful lesions on both legs. She reported chills, bilateral lower extremity swelling, and several small, painful, 'pimple-like bumps' appearing on her bilateral lower legs, which ulcerated several days later. The ulcers progressed despite a recent course of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for cultures growing methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus. Medical history includes treatment with methimazole and atenolol for the past year. No other medications or supplements were reported.

exams.source_report: Bilateral lower extremities revealed pitting edema and multiple discrete, round, dry ulcers, most with central eschars, dusky gray borders, and collarettes of scale. During follow-up, an intact 4-mm papular lesion was identified on her lower right leg. No pathergy at the previous punch biopsy site was observed.

initial: A man underwent placement of a lumbar catheter to drain cerebrospinal fluid at the start of a vascular surgery procedure. On the first postoperative day, the drain was removed by an anesthesia resident. On postoperative day 6, the patient reported persistent drainage from the lumbar drain site since hospital discharge.

exams.source_report: Examination revealed a raised area of skin with clear fluid at the lumbar drain site.

tests.source_report: Imaging studies: Imaging confirmed the presence of a foreign body at the lumbar drain site.

initial: A white woman in her 60s with history of bone marrow transplant in 2014. Current medications include oral azathioprine (50 mg twice daily), tacrolimus (0.5 mg twice daily), prednisone (25 mg daily), monthly intravenous immunoglobulin, prophylactic oral fluconazole, acyclovir, sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim, and penicillin. One month prior to starting azathioprine, patient developed nodules on the genital and perianal region, with 1 ulcerated nodule in the perianal area associated with painless bleeding on trauma. The lesions were otherwise asymptomatic.

exams.source_report: Several yellow-colored nodules present, some ulcerated with extrusion of yellow-colored discharge on the left labia majora and perianal area with surrounding inflammatory reaction. Additional findings include sclerodermatous plaques on lower legs, scarring alopecia on scalp with minimal hyperkeratosis, nail dystrophy and lichenoid changes, erythematous changes in both feet, and desquamation in the lower legs, back and arms.

tests.source_report:
- Laboratory tests: White blood cell count of 13.1 × 103/μL. Full blood count, electrolytes, urea and creatinine, and liver function tests were stable and unremarkable.
  - Histopathology: Excisional biopsy showed focal ulceration and acute inflammation in the epithelium. Deep nodular aggregates of granular histiocytes and neutrophils present. Round calcospherites observed. Positive staining with von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stain. No fungi or mycobacteria seen on silver and Ziehl-Neelsen stain. No dysplasia or malignancy.
  - Microbiology: Bacterial culture showed heavy growth of Escherichia coli.
  - Images:
    Image Title: Clinical photographs of cutaneous nodules
    Image Description: A) Multiple erythematous eroded nodules in the perianal area. B) Yellowish nodules located on the left labia majora.

initial: A man in his 20s presented with an 8-month history of multiple reddish papules on the right forearm, wrist, and scalp that had developed 2 months after a road traffic collision over the ensuing posttraumatic scars. The papules occasionally bled on minor trauma.

exams.source_report: There were 5 erythematous-to-violaceous vascular-appearing papules grouped on the right forearm near the elbow, 1 similar reddish plaque on the ipsilateral wrist, and a nodule on the temporal scalp. All lesions were present on the background of posttraumatic dyspigmentation and scarring.

initial: A man in his 60s presented with severe fatigue. His medical history was significant for primary hyperparathyroidism 6 years prior to presentation, for which the patient refused therapeutic management. The patient was cachectic and exhibited significant muscular weakness.

exams.source_report: Clinical examination revealed a large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger that had gradually enlarged in recent months.

initial: A 61-year-old woman with severe, recalcitrant condition affecting multiple areas of skin. Previous treatments included topical agents, UV light, methotrexate, acitretin, and adalimumab, which were unsuccessful. Initial treatment with secukinumab led to complete clearance within 2 months. After 3 months of secukinumab treatment, she developed new symptoms affecting her fingernails.

exams.source_report: Patient presented with severe, disabling fingernail dystrophy and distal onychopathy in previously normal nails. The fingertips were also affected. Toes were unaffected.

initial: A woman in her 80s presented with a 1-week history of progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin. She reported enlargement of the tongue over the past 3 months, leading to difficulty with mastication. She also experienced numbness without weakness of her distal lower limbs for 3 months, which restricted her mobility requiring diapers. Her medical history included IgG λ-type multiple myeloma complicated by anemia and lytic lesions in the calvarium, managed conservatively with transfusions. She was taking folic acid and intramuscular cyanocobalamin supplements due to deficiencies attributed to dietary cause.

exams.source_report: Circinate purpuric patches with erosions on the natal cleft, buttocks, inguinal creases, and vulva. Hemorrhagic flaccid bullae on the posterior perineum. Macroglossia, glossitis, and a hemorrhagic erosion on the hard palate. Purpuric macules present periorbitally, on the lips, inframammary folds, forearms, and thighs.

exams.source_report: Examination demonstrated waxy yellow papules and plaques with purpura in the periocular, neck, axillary, trunk, and inguinal regions.

initial: A patient in their 40s with a history of hypertension and smoking presented to the emergency department with sudden-onset palpitations and chest tightness after an argument. The symptoms relieved spontaneously after 50 minutes. The patient was asymptomatic on arrival.

initial: A 33-year-old male soldier experienced syncope while deployed overseas. The episode occurred after prolonged standing in a warm environment, with prodromal symptoms of lightheadedness, greying out, diaphoresis, and fatigue. Loss of consciousness lasted less than 30 seconds, followed by a head strike. After regaining consciousness, he experienced several hours of severe headache, clouded thought, and some memory loss. He had multiple near-syncopal events without loss of consciousness over the previous 2 years, each preceded by similar symptoms and associated with prolonged standing. His history was unremarkable, and he was not taking any medications. He denied episodes with exertion, dehydration, emotional stress, or other activities.

exams.source_report: Cardiology examination was unremarkable, with no murmurs, gallops, unequal pulses, or neurologic abnormalities.

tests.source_report: - Laboratory tests: No anemia, electrolyte abnormalities, or abnormal thyroid function.- Cardiac monitoring:  * ECG showed normal sinus rhythm  * 2-week cardiac event monitor showed no evidence of arrhythmias or pathologic block at rest or with activity  * Graded exercise treadmill test showed excellent functional capacity, appropriate heart rate and blood pressure augmentation with exercise, no exercise-induced arrhythmias or chronotropic incompetence- Imaging:  * Transthoracic echocardiogram showed no valvular abnormalities, normal systolic and diastolic function (ejection fraction 55%-60%), normal left and right ventricular chamber dimensions- Special tests:  * Drug-free tilt-table test induced syncope with ECG showing profound sinus bradycardia to 30 beats per minute, transition to junctional bradycardia during presyncope, followed by sinus pause with >6-second pauses without associated escape rhythm during syncope

initial: A man in his 40s, weighing 109kg, with stage IV KRAS wild-type rectal adenocarcinoma diagnosed in November 2013. He had pulmonary and liver metastases. His treatment history included radiation therapy and multiple chemotherapy cycles. In December 2014, he was enrolled in trial E7208 at the Smilow Cancer Hospital at Yale-New Haven and was randomized to receive combination therapy every 2 weeks.

exams.source_report: In early January 2015, the patient developed a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias on his lower right lateral shin, which grew to 4 cm. The lesion was not associated with pain or pruritus.

initial: A man in his 50s presented with pink-purple dermal papules and polyarticular inflammatory arthritis involving the wrists, metacarpophalangeal joints, and proximal interphalangeal joints. He experienced fatigue, dyspnea on exertion, and reported a 5-7 kg weight loss without fever or sweats. His pulmonary and joint symptoms were relieved by daily oral prednisone and flared with taper below 10 mg. Previous treatments included hydroxychloroquine 400 mg daily for 18 months and weekly adalimumab injections for 7 months, without improvement.

exams.source_report: Numerous pink-purple dermal papules were present on the trunk and extremities, with preference for the extensor surfaces of the arms and legs. No lymphadenopathy was noted.

tests.source_report: - Laboratory tests: Complete blood cell count, metabolic panel, hemoglobin A1c, viral and rheumatologic panels (including HIV), and serum/urine protein electrophoresis were normal or unremarkable.- Imaging studies:  - Chest radiograph: Normal  - High-resolution chest CT scan: Unremarkable  - Hand radiographs: Normal  - Echocardiography: Normal- Pulmonary Function Tests: Revealed mild restrictive disease with decreased forced vital capacity and total lung capacity- Pathology:  Image Title: Skin Biopsy Findings  Image Description: A) Pink-purple papules on extensor surface of arms  B) Nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate (H&E stain)  C) Admixed atypical, irregularly contoured lymphocytes with numerous histiocytes  D) Low CD4 signal and robust CD8 signal (20x magnification)- Additional Testing:  - T-cell receptor PCR: Matching clonal rearrangements identified in 3 skin biopsy specimens and bone marrow sample  - Flow cytometry of bone marrow: Revealed lymphocytes with atypical CD3-negative, CD4-negative, CD5-positive, CD8-positive phenotype (2% of total cells)  - Immunostaining: Lymphocytes positive for CD3, inverted CD8:CD4 ratio, predominantly α/β positive

Neurological examination initially normal at baseline. Two days after procedure, patient presented with status epilepticus and left upper extremity weakness. Follow-up neurological examination at 6 months showed full strength in the upper and lower extremities and normal tone.

Medical history was noncontributory, and she was taking no regular medications.

initial: A 48-year-old man initially presented with a lesion on the scalp. After wide local excision and skin graft, extensive pigmented plaques and nodules grew within months around the graft site. Patient had previously received 3 cycles of pembrolizumab followed by 5 treatments of TVEC (3-4 mL total volume per treatment, injecting 3 largest areas in first cycle and 6 areas in next 4 cycles). Patient reported malaise after the fifth treatment.

exams.source_report: Numerous black smooth macules and patches were observed within and outside the graft. Dermoscopy revealed diffuse black structureless pigment sparing follicular and eccrine units.

initial: A woman in her 30s with a history of right breast cancer, stage IIIa (cT2N2M0). She underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by right modified radical mastectomy and postoperative radiotherapy. After radiotherapy, she noticed a pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site of the right breast. The lesion did not respond to initial topical treatments. Three months later (1 year after initial cancer diagnosis), she presented to dermatology for evaluation of skin erythema over her right breast.

exams.source_report: A well-demarcated, warm, erythematous plaque, 15 × 12 cm, was seen over the right side of the anterior chest wall around her operation scar. Scattered within the erythema were multiple palpable small nodules.

initial: A previously healthy 17-year-old male presented with 3 days of mouth pain and nonpainful penile erosions. One week prior, he experienced transient anosmia and ageusia that had spontaneously resolved. He denied fever, cough, dyspnea, rhinorrhea, and gastrointestinal symptoms. He had taken acetaminophen and ibuprofen before presenting to the emergency department, but no medications before the onset of his mucocutaneous eruption.

exams.source_report: Patient was afebrile and in no distress. Vital signs were normal, including respiratory rate of 16 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation of 97%. Examination revealed:- Shallow erosions of the vermilion lips and hard palate- Circumferential erythematous erosions of the periurethral glans penis - 5 small vesicles on the trunk and upper extremitiesThe remainder of the mucocutaneous (including palms and soles), cervical lymphatic, and cardiopulmonary examinations were unremarkable.

initial: A man in his 60s presented with a lesion on the left lower eyelid. His ocular history was notable for a traumatic icicle injury as a child that resulted in loss of the left eye. He had surgery to place an implant into the eye socket, and approximately 14 years prior underwent a lower eyelid reconstruction. He had excellent prosthesis position without need for refitting or replacement for more than 10 years until recently noting that his ocular prosthesis would spontaneously extrude from his anophthalmic socket.

exams.source_report: On examination, he had a small, pearly lesion in the tear trough region of the left lower eyelid that had been growing over the past few months. He had contraction of the conjunctival mucosal tissue across the fornix of the left lower eyelid and increased scleral show of his ocular prosthesis with shortening of his lower eyelid skin. His prosthesis was extruded from his socket due to cicatricial effects causing conjunctival shrinkage and eyelid skin contracture.

initial: A man in his 70s presented with a 2-week history of a bullous eruption localized to the hands and feet. He denied having pruritus or spontaneous bleeding but reported discomfort from the pressure of intact bullae. Medical history included diabetes mellitus and hypertension, well controlled with a stable regimen of lisinopril and atenolol for several years. He denied using any new medications or supplements or making recent dose adjustments in existing medications. No history of prior bullous eruption.

exams.source_report: Numerous small intact bullae and large erosions on the lateral feet, soles, and toes. The extent of the bullae led to difficulty with ambulation. Intact vesicles present on the lateral palms along with erosions demonstrating evidence of previous bullae formation. No vesicular or bullous lesions on the trunk, arms, legs, or mucosal surfaces.

initial: A man in his 70s with a 6-year history of psoriasiform dermatitis presented with worsening of his eruption and new eroded and noneroded nodules on his forehead. His condition had been partially controlled with topical corticosteroids, methotrexate (20 mg/wk), acitretin (25 mg/d), and narrowband UV-B phototherapy 3 times weekly. Two months prior, he developed widespread molluscum contagiosum, with negative HIV screening. He denied systemic symptoms including weight loss, fevers, and/or chills. Medical history included multiple nonmelanoma skin cancers (basal and squamous cell carcinomas), in situ melanoma on the back, ocular melanoma, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes mellitus.

initial: An asymptomatic male patient in his 40s with no relevant ocular, medical, or family history was referred for assessment of a retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) defect in his right eye by an optometrist. Over the next 4 years of monitoring, he remained largely asymptomatic, except for mild metamorphopsia reported on his most recent assessment.

During follow-up examinations, the PED in his right eye persisted largely unchanged, with two notable occasions where the PED resolved and then relapsed within an hour during clinic visits.

initial: A woman in her early 70s with acral lentiginous melanoma on her heel was initially treated with wide excision and sentinel lymph node resection followed by ipilimumab therapy. Prior to cycle 4 of therapy, she had nodal recurrence requiring resection. Four weeks after her maintenance dose, the patient developed decreased vision, mild photophobia, and ocular tenderness on palpation in each eye. Review of systems revealed nausea, itchiness, and weight loss.

exams.source_report: Visual acuity was 20/40 OU and she had bilateral multifocal serous retinal detachments without signs of inflammation. After 1 month, the fundus showed accumulation of yellowish subretinal material with increased autofluorescence.

initial: A man in his 70s presented with 2 progressively enlarging, painless nodular lesions on the forehead and right cheek, initially observed as erythematous nodules 3 months prior. Dermoscopy showed arborizing telangiectasias, central ulceration with crusting, and peripheral pigment. No additional lesions or abnormalities were found on examination of surrounding skin and general systemic evaluation.
